scored.title: Artificial intelligence-based diagnostic decision support for primary care of older adults using collective intelligence and imitation learning.
scored.why: Investigators trained a multi-label neural network on 707,598 primary care encounters of adults 65 and older using imitation learning to mimic clinician diagnostic and ordering decisions, then validated it with a randomized, blinded equivalence study showing diagnostic recommendations were statistically equivalent to actual clinician practice, though order recommendations were not. This is one of the few diagnostic decision support system (DDSS) studies to move beyond retrospective discrimination metrics to a prospective clinician-comparison design, which is exactly the kind of evidence this reader should track even though order-level equivalence failed.

scored.title: AI-based delineation based on clinical data in MR-guided brachytherapy for cervical cancer reduces delineation time - A prospective paired trial.
scored.why: A prospective paired trial in 32 patients undergoing MR-guided cervical cancer brachytherapy used an nnU-Net deep learning model trained on uncurated clinical data to auto-delineate organs at risk, reducing delineation time by 31% (10.1 minutes, 95% confidence interval (CI) 7.4-12) with a median surface distance under 2.1 mm from clinician-corrected contours. This is a real prospective clinical workflow deployment with a measured time-efficiency benefit in a reproductive cancer setting, which is a stronger evidentiary bar than the retrospective segmentation studies typical of this literature.

scored.title: Safety-Oriented Benchmarking of Large Language Models in Risk-Based Management of Abnormal Cervical Screening Results: Scenario-Based Benchmark Study.
scored.why: This benchmark study tested three large language models (LLMs) on 60 synthetic scenarios of abnormal cervical screening management against American Society for Colposcopy and Cervical Pathology (ASCCP) guidelines, finding unsafe major error-free rates ranging from 75 percent (DeepSeek V3.2) to 100 percent (GPT-5.3) under a guideline-directed prompt, with error rates rising sharply with scenario complexity. The blinded, gynecologist-rated safety framework with quantified error subtypes is a more rigorous evaluation than typical chatbot-quality rubrics, though scenarios are synthetic rather than real patient cases.

scored.title: The Alignment Paradox of Medical Large Language Models in Infertility Care: Decoupling Algorithmic Improvement From Clinical Decision-Making Quality.
scored.why: This retrospective study of 8201 infertility electronic health records compared four large language model (LLM) alignment strategies, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), group relative policy optimization (GRPO), and in-context learning (ICL), finding that GRPO scored highest on automatic metrics but blinded expert review by two reproductive medicine specialists rated the simpler SFT model higher on reasoning and treatment feasibility, with SFT selected as the best response in 51.2 percent of cases versus 26.2 percent for GRPO. This decoupling of automatic benchmark performance from expert clinical judgment is a genuinely useful and underappreciated finding for anyone building or evaluating clinical decision-support LLMs in reproductive medicine.

scored.title: Implicit Bias in Large Language Model Diagnosis of Eating Disorders: Experimental Vignette Study.
scored.why: This experimental vignette study tested 10 large language model (LLM) configurations on 1152 matched synthetic clinical cases and found substantial demographic bias in psychiatric diagnosis, including a 9.57 odds ratio for Latine patients receiving a major depressive disorder (MDD) diagnosis over identical White-patient vignettes, using mixed-effects logistic regression. This is a clear, well-controlled failure-mode demonstration relevant to the reader's interest in how language models err when reasoning about patients, though it is limited to synthetic vignettes rather than real clinical encounters.

scored.title: Teal Health Secures $22M for At-Home HPV Cervical Cancer Screening Device
scored.why: Teal Health raised a $22 million Series A funding round led by .406 Ventures for its at-home human papillomavirus (HPV) cervical cancer screening device, with participation from several named venture firms. This is a concrete capital event tied to a specific product aimed at expanding cervical cancer screening access, which is squarely within scope for tracking industry movement in women's health.

scored.title: Comparative evaluation of ambient digital scribe systems in clinical documentation.
scored.why: This study compared three commercial ambient digital scribe (ADS) systems on two simulated clinical encounters, pairing 56 physicians' Likert ratings with an independent transcript-level error audit, and found that the vendor with the highest clinician ratings was not the one with the fewest audited errors, suggesting clinicians' subjective judgments and objective accuracy diverge. The exploratory sample size and single simulated encounter type limit generalizability, but the mismatch between perceived quality and factual accuracy is a useful caution for anyone evaluating scribe tools by survey alone.

scored.title: Trastuzumab plus nivolumab with gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line therapy for HER2-positive unresectable biliary tract cancer: a phase 1b/2 trial.
scored.why: This phase 1b/2 trial of trastuzumab plus nivolumab with gemcitabine and cisplatin in HER2 (human epidermal growth factor receptor 2)-positive biliary tract cancer reported a 55% objective response rate and median progression-free survival of 10.6 months, with a preplanned artificial intelligence-powered whole-slide image analysis suggesting higher HER2 3+ cell proportions correlated with greater benefit. The trial itself is a substantive first-line readout worth tracking for oncology, but the AI component is a secondary, exploratory biomarker analysis rather than the study's main contribution.

scored.title: A RISKmilk framework for predicting drug and chemical exposure in human milk during breastfeeding.
scored.why: Researchers built RISKmilk, a machine learning-enhanced physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model that predicts drug transfer into breast milk from molecular structure, improving the proportion of predictions within twofold error from 29.6% to 66.4% compared to a conventional equation-based benchmark, and applied it to screen marketed drugs for lactation risk. This is a methodologically substantive advance for an underserved population in drug safety modeling, though it remains a computational prediction tool without prospective clinical validation.

scored.title: Large Language Models Meet Gynecologic Ultrasound: Advancing the Characterization of ADNEXal Masses.
scored.why: Investigators tested ChatGPT (GPT-5) on classifying 300 adnexal masses as benign or malignant against the IOTA (International Ovarian Tumor Analysis) Simple Rules, the ADNEX model, and expert subjective assessment, with the language model reaching about 73-75% accuracy compared to 87.3% for expert assessment. This is a genuine head-to-head comparison of a large language model (LLM) against established clinical decision tools and human experts, meeting the bar for the language-model beat, though the model underperformed experts and needs further validation before clinical use.

scored.title: Distinct clinical patterns of preterm infants vulnerable to intestinal injury identified by unsupervised clustering.
scored.why: Using unsupervised hierarchical clustering on a prospective cohort of 20,352 very low birth weight infants from the Korean Neonatal Network, this study identified eight clinical clusters and five subclusters of intestinal injury independent of standard necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) diagnostic labels, with survival patterns validated against a supervised model. The large multicenter scale and diagnosis-independent phenotyping offer a potentially useful reframing of NEC heterogeneity, though the work remains exploratory and lacks external validation outside the network.

scored.title: Large language model-based triage to identify antiretroviral therapy adherence barriers and risk levels in patient messages.
scored.why: Researchers fine-tuned large language models (LLMs), including Flan-T5 and clinical foundation models, on 15,480 annotated patient message sentences from people with HIV to detect antiretroviral therapy (ART) adherence barriers and stratify nonadherence risk, with Flan-T5-xl achieving a Macro-F1 of 0.83 internally and 0.71 on an external dataset while using roughly 30 times less energy than GPT-4.1. This is a real patient-message classification task with external validation and a fairness and environmental-footprint analysis, which is more substantive than a typical chatbot-quality rubric study, though it stops short of clinical deployment.

scored.title: Improving patient communication and understanding of medical reports through text simplification with ChatGPT: a comparative study.
scored.why: In this study, ChatGPT simplified five types of medical reports, including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), surgical, pathology, and discharge summaries, and 576 laypeople without medical training were tested on comprehension of either the original or simplified version, with simplified reports improving comprehension accuracy substantially, for example from 53.7 percent to 80.3 percent on MRI reports. Unlike most chatbot-quality rubric studies, this measures an actual downstream effect on patient understanding with a large sample, which makes it more informative for this beat despite lacking a clinician-generated simplification comparator.

scored.title: Automated Brief Hospital Course Summarization in Cardiac Surgery Using a Lightweight Large Language Model-Based Framework: Development and Evaluation Study on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV.
scored.why: This study developed LiteMedDoc, a lightweight, locally deployable large language model (LLM) pipeline built on an 8-billion-parameter open-source model, to automatically generate brief hospital course (BHC) summaries for 4538 coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) cases from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-IV database, evaluated with both standard natural language processing (NLP) metrics and a clinical review by 15 cardiac surgeons rating completeness, correctness, and quality. The combination of a privacy-preserving local deployment design, a meaningful clinical documentation burden target, and genuine clinician rating rather than just rubric scoring makes this a more substantive contribution than typical chatbot-quality papers.

scored.title: A real-time machine learning framework for improved intraoperative risk predictions in cardiac surgery patients.
scored.why: A retrospective single-center cohort of 6416 cardiac surgery patients trained an end-to-end transformer model (TE-Transformer) that ingests preoperative, intraoperative, and note data to produce continuously updated multitask risk predictions, reporting area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.85 for mortality and 0.88 for delirium, outperforming XGBoost and recurrent neural network baselines. The study lacks external or prospective validation, so its clinical utility for real-time decision support remains unproven despite the architectural novelty.

scored.title: A co-learning framework for maternal and pediatric pharmacotherapy knowledge gap discovery.
scored.why: This study built a co-learning framework combining active learning and large language model (LLM) fine-tuning to classify 38 million PubMed abstracts into pharmacokinetics, pharmaco-epidemiology, and clinical trial categories, achieving F1-scores up to 0.96 with external validation, and found that 22 to 66 percent of drugs prescribed in pregnancy lack pharmacokinetic or pharmaco-epidemiologic evidence. The methodology is rigorous with genuine external validation, but the output is a literature landscaping tool rather than a patient-facing or clinically deployed AI system.

scored.title: Unsupervised machine learning for free water-eliminated diffusion tensor imaging of the fetal brain.
scored.why: This study developed an unsupervised machine learning method for free water-eliminated diffusion tensor imaging (FWE-DTI) of the fetal brain, trained on research-quality fetal and neonatal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data and independently validated on lower-quality external data, showing reduced estimation error for fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity compared to conventional methods. The technical improvement in tissue microstructure characterization could aid fetal brain development research, though clinical outcome relevance and broader validation remain to be established.

scored.title: A co-learning framework for maternal and pediatric pharmacotherapy knowledge gap discovery.
scored.why: This study built a co-learning framework combining active learning and large language model (LLM) fine-tuning to classify 38 million PubMed abstracts into pharmacokinetics, pharmaco-epidemiology, and clinical trial categories, achieving F1-scores up to 0.96 with external validation, and found that 22 to 66 percent of drugs prescribed in pregnancy lack pharmacokinetic or pharmaco-epidemiologic evidence. The methodology is rigorous with genuine external validation, but the output is a literature landscaping tool rather than a patient-facing or clinically deployed AI system.

scored.title: MRI-based fetal gestational age estimation using a structure-aware self-supervised network.
scored.why: A structure-aware self-supervised deep learning model estimated fetal gestational age (GA) from 1630 fetal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans across 207 singleton pregnancies, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.79 weeks and R-squared of 0.934 on an internal held-out test set. The result is promising but remains single-center and retrospective without external or multi-site validation, limiting confidence that it generalizes.

scored.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review of Emerging Clinical Applications in Patient Communication and Education, Documentation, and Decision Support.
scored.why: This systematic review synthesized 23 studies on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in total hip and knee arthroplasty, finding that blinded clinician ratings judged ChatGPT-generated answers to patient frequently asked questions (FAQs) as comparable in accuracy, clarity, and completeness to surgeon-written responses, and that large language models (LLMs) achieved 97.5 to 100 percent accuracy identifying operative report information. The review aggregates existing single-study comparisons without new data or risk-of-bias assessment, but it does include the kind of clinician-comparator evidence the reader values, making it moderately useful as a field summary.

scored.title: Semantic Similarity Search Approach to Extract Exemplars of Stigmatizing and Positive Language in Obstetric Clinical Notes: Exploratory Study.
scored.why: This exploratory study used a semantic similarity search approach to find exemplars of stigmatizing and positive language in obstetric clinical notes from two US hospitals, achieving 69 percent average precision at a cosine similarity threshold of 0.75, with weaker performance for stigmatizing categories like 'difficult patient' language. The approach reduces annotation burden but the modest precision, especially for the categories most relevant to bias detection, limits its immediate utility.

scored.title: Deep Generative and Graph-Based Representation Learning for Multiomics Survival Stratification in Ovarian Cancer: Secondary Analysis.
scored.why: This secondary analysis used variational autoencoders (VAEs) to derive latent representations from multiomics data of 291 ovarian cancer patients in The Cancer Genome Atlas, identifying two survival-distinct clusters (hazard ratio 0.519, 95% confidence interval 0.343-0.785). The proposed graph convolutional network extension was not actually evaluated, and the retrospective single-database design without independent validation limits clinical applicability.

scored.title: Improved upper abdominal MRI with VIBE sequences using deep learning-supported k-space sampling in a cohort undergoing MRI for gynecologic diseases.
scored.why: In a prospective study of 60 women undergoing pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), a deep learning-supported k-space reconstruction method for volumetric interpolated breath-hold examination (VIBE) sequences improved subjective image quality and reduced artifacts compared to standard VIBE, though quantitative signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) showed no significant difference. The prospective design and radiologist ratings are reasonable, but the sample is modest and the finding is an incremental image-quality improvement rather than a diagnostic or outcome-changing result.

scored.title: Preparing AI chatbots to respond to patient distress and suicidality in high-risk healthcare settings.
scored.why: This paper describes suicide safety monitoring features built into a chatbot deployed in a high-risk clinical setting and offers design recommendations, but it presents no comparative evaluation, outcome data, or measured effect on patient safety. As a descriptive framework rather than an empirical study, it falls short of the evidentiary bar this reader needs for the language-model-patient beat, though the topic itself is important.

scored.title: A Systematic Review of the Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems for Assessing Multiple Parameters During the Ultrasound Evaluation of Fetal Growth.
scored.why: This systematic review synthesizes 19 studies covering more than 730,000 ultrasound images assessing AI systems for multi-parameter fetal biometry, concluding favorable but heterogeneous performance without standardized reporting or prospective multicenter validation. As a review rather than new primary evidence, it mainly reorganizes known limitations rather than advancing the field.

scored.title: Metals and metalloids signatures in early pregnancy suggest cadmium and arsenic as major mixture components associated with gestational diabetes mellitus risk.
scored.why: This prospective cohort of 1201 pregnant women in China measured urinary metal and metalloid levels and used machine learning, with XGBoost performing best, to modestly improve discrimination for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) risk beyond conventional biochemical markers. The AI component is incidental to what is primarily an environmental epidemiology and toxicology study, and the modest discrimination gain limits its practical impact.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence for women's reproductive health: A scoping review of global diagnostic trends, methodological gaps, and a translational research agenda for low-resource settings.
scored.why: This scoping review of 116 studies on artificial intelligence in women's reproductive and endocrine health finds that 83.6% carry high risk of bias and 75.5% lack external validation, with stark geographic inequities in research output between high-income and low-resource settings. The paper proposes a feasibility framework for low-resource deployment but presents no new primary evidence, so it functions as a field-mapping and gap-analysis exercise rather than a finding that changes practice.

scored.title: Perinatal Mental Health Detection and Prediction Using Mobile Sensing Data: Systematic Review.
scored.why: This systematic review of 10 studies on mobile sensing for perinatal mental health found high discrimination metrics for postpartum depression detection in individual studies, area under the curve (AUC) values up to 0.87, but rated 80% of assessment units at high risk of bias due to small samples and limited validation. The review concludes current evidence does not support clinical screening use, making it a useful orientation piece rather than a practice-changing result.

scored.title: Clinical challenges in the adaptation of AI predictive models in radiation oncology for gynaecological cancer: a systematic review by the radiation oncology-AI MITO group.
scored.why: This systematic review of 31 studies on AI predictive models in gynecologic radiotherapy found that only two of 31 studies (6.5%) performed external validation, and 41.9% carried high risk of bias by CHARMS (Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews of Prediction Modelling Studies) criteria, concentrated mostly in cervical cancer. As a review documenting known translational gaps rather than new primary results, it is useful for context but not a driver of new clinical action.

scored.title: Generative AI Utilization and Perspectives Among Reproductive-Age Women with Systemic Autoimmune and Rheumatic Diseases.
scored.why: A cross-sectional survey of 190 reproductive-age women with systemic autoimmune and rheumatic diseases (SARDs) found high familiarity with generative artificial intelligence but low actual use for health questions, with strong preference for physician-endorsed tools, particularly around medication safety in pregnancy and lactation. This is a usage-attitudes survey without any model performance evaluation, so it belongs to the routine tier for the language-model-patient beat despite its relevance to reproductive care.

scored.title: Identification of key molecular targets in nicotine-induced spontaneous abortion through network toxicology and multi-omics integration.
scored.why: This bioinformatics study integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, machine learning, Mendelian randomization (MR), and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify five hub genes linked to nicotine-induced spontaneous abortion, with two genes showing causal associations by Mendelian randomization. The work is mechanistic and computational rather than a clinical AI application with patient-facing evaluation, so it sits at the periphery of this reader's core beats despite its reproductive health relevance.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence in Semen Analysis and Sperm Selection: Opportunities and Challenges.
scored.why: This is a narrative review summarizing existing applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in semen analysis, sperm selection, and outcome prediction in andrology, concluding that most studies suffer from small datasets and lack of external validation. No new data or evaluation is presented, so it functions as a survey of the field rather than a finding that would change practice.

scored.title: Prevalence, associated factors, and machine learning classification of low back pain among postmenopausal women attending rehabilitation and physiotherapy facilities in Bangladesh.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study of 566 postmenopausal Bangladeshi women used multiple machine learning classifiers, including support vector machine and random forest, to classify low back pain, with the best model reaching an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.890 on a held-out test set. The design is a single-population cross-sectional survey with no clinical deployment or external validation, and the AI component adds little beyond the epidemiological association analysis.

scored.title: Flatfoot and artificial intelligence: Can language models be trusted for patient education?
scored.why: This cross-sectional study compared ChatGPT and Google Gemini responses to 15 patient questions about flatfoot, rated by two orthopedic surgeons on accuracy, added value, omissions, and readability, with Gemini scoring higher on all measures. This is a rubric-based chatbot comparison without a clinician-generated answer comparator or measurement of real patient understanding, making it routine for this beat.

scored.title: Comparative Evaluation of a New Autonomous AI Agent Versus Frontier LLMs for AI-Generated Patient Information Sheets on Pediatric Pathologies.
scored.why: This study compared an autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agent against several frontier large language models (LLMs) in generating patient information sheets for pediatric oral pathology, scored by three expert evaluators using standard quality and readability instruments including the Global Quality Score (GQS) and DISCERN. As with similar chatbot-comparison studies, this evaluates rubric-based quality among AI systems without a clinician-authored comparator or measure of actual patient comprehension, making it routine for this beat.

scored.title: Quality and Readability of Four AI Chatbots Answering Search-Derived Patient Questions About Primary Aldosteronism: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study.
scored.why: Four chatbot configurations, including GPT-5.5, Copilot, Gemini, and Perplexity, were compared on responses to 17 patient questions about primary aldosteronism using structural quality instruments like DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA benchmarks, and Global Quality Score, with the authors explicitly noting these tools do not assess factual accuracy. This is another rubric-only chatbot comparison without a clinician baseline or patient comprehension outcome, placing it squarely in the routine category for this beat.

scored.title: The readability and quality paradox: Comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity outputs on pediatric chest pain queries.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study compared ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity on readability and quality of responses to pediatric chest pain queries using standard instruments like the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), modified DISCERN, and Global Quality Score (GQS), finding all models scored above the recommended sixth-grade reading level and that quality and readability often traded off. This is a routine rubric-based chatbot comparison without a clinician comparator or measured effect on patient understanding.

scored.title: Generative AI responses to exercise-related questions asked by patients with multiple sclerosis: An evaluation of quality, accuracy, and readability.
scored.why: This study compared ChatGPT-5.4 and Google Gemini 3 Flash on 75 exercise-related questions from multiple sclerosis (MS) patients, rated by physiotherapists using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN, a Likert accuracy scale, and Flesch Reading Ease (FRE), finding ChatGPT outperformed Gemini on quality and accuracy while both scored poorly on readability. This is a rubric-based comparison between two chatbots without a clinician-generated answer comparator or a measured effect on patient behavior or understanding, making it routine for this beat.

scored.title: Evaluation of the accuracy and reproducibility of large language models (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini) in responding to patient-centered lipedema questions.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study compared ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Gemini on accuracy and reproducibility for 25 patient-facing lipedema questions, rated by three experts using a four-point scale, with DeepSeek scoring highest at 72% comprehensive-and-correct. It has no clinician-generated comparator and is a rubric-based benchmark of the kind the reader already expects, limiting its news value despite decent methodology.

scored.title: Evaluating the accuracy and comprehensiveness of GPT-4 as a patient information tool for pectus deformities.
scored.why: This study evaluated GPT-4 responses to 99 frequently asked patient questions about pectus deformities, rated by a physiatrist and pediatric surgeon on a four-point scale, finding 51.5% correct and comprehensive with no clinician comparator arm. It is a routine rubric-based accuracy check of the type the reader is already familiar with, offering limited new insight.

scored.title: Beyond one-size-fits-all: mapping information-seeking and decision-making pathways in cancer care.
scored.why: This cross-sectional survey of 205 Israeli cancer patients used cluster analysis to identify four information-seeking archetypes and found that reliance on generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools remained consistently low across groups. The study is descriptive and exploratory with no clinician comparison or intervention, making it more background context than a substantive finding for this beat.

scored.title: Exploring young adult cancer survivors' perspectives on generative AI chatbots for symptom support.
scored.why: This qualitative descriptive study interviewed 18 young adult cancer survivors about their perspectives on generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for symptom support, identifying themes around personalization, trust, and oversight. It reports attitudes and preferences rather than measured performance, accuracy, or comparison to clinicians, limiting its relevance for evaluating actual chatbot capability.

scored.title: Machine learning prediction of pregnancy outcomes after vitrified-warmed bovine embryo transfer using field-derived variables.
scored.why: This exploratory study applied six machine learning models to 236 vitrified-warmed bovine embryo transfer records, with random forest achieving only modest discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) 0.703) for predicting pregnancy outcome. The work is veterinary, small, and internally validated only, placing it outside the reader's human reproductive medicine focus and of limited standalone interest.

scored.title: Male infertility research for the ART clinic: priorities to enhance patient outcomes, education and wellbeing.
scored.why: This narrative review discusses priorities for male infertility research in assisted reproductive technology (ART) clinics, covering paternal genetics, fertility awareness, and psychosocial support, with artificial intelligence mentioned only as one of several search terms rather than a substantive focus. It contains no primary data, algorithmic method, or evaluation, making it off-topic for the AI-focused reproductive beat despite its clinical relevance.

scored.title: Opportunities and Challenges for PBPK Modelling in Specific Populations: Considerations for Paediatrics, Pregnancy, Lactation, Ethnic Differences, and Organ Impairment.
scored.why: This book chapter reviews the general use of physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling across special populations including pregnancy, lactation, and pediatrics, without presenting new data, a specific model, or an evaluation. It is a broad educational overview rather than a research finding, placing it at the low end of relevance for this digest.

scored.title: Obstetric pharmacoeconomics.
scored.why: This is a review of obstetric pharmacoeconomics covering cost-effectiveness analysis and value-based maternal therapeutics, mentioning artificial intelligence only briefly among many other topics without presenting original data or an evaluated AI system. It has essentially no algorithmic component and functions as a broad opinion and policy overview rather than a research finding.

scored.title: Development of an Equity-Centered Sociotechnical Architecture for Generative AI Integration in Public Health Promotion: Conceptual Framework.
scored.why: This is a viewpoint proposing a conceptual sociotechnical framework for generative AI (GenAI) in public health communication, based on a narrative synthesis of literature rather than original data or evaluation. It offers no empirical comparison, deployment, or measured outcome, making it low-value for a reader tracking evidence on language models and patients.

scored.title: Generative artificial intelligence-assisted medical self-care and associated factors among undergraduate students at Arsi University, South-Eastern Ethiopia.
scored.why: This cross-sectional survey of 414 Ethiopian undergraduates measured self-reported prevalence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-assisted self-medication and its associated demographic factors using logistic regression, finding 70% engagement and several odds ratios for predictors. It contains no clinician comparison, patient message analysis, or outcome measure relevant to clinical AI communication, making it peripheral to this beat.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence for Lacrimal Drainage Disorders: Advances in Diagnosis, Management, and Clinical Translation.
scored.why: This is a narrative review summarizing existing machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and large language model (LLM) applications to lacrimal drainage disorders, without new data or clinical validation. It is a survey of the field rather than a study with a measurable finding, and has minimal relevance to reproductive medicine or patient-facing LLM evaluation.

scored.title: [Generative artificial intelligence and language models in trauma surgery : Applications in clinical care, research and teaching].
scored.why: This narrative literature review discusses generative artificial intelligence (AI) and large language model (LLM) applications in trauma surgery documentation, decision support, and teaching, without presenting new empirical data or comparisons. It offers general commentary rather than a measurable finding relevant to patient-facing evaluation.

scored.title: Generative AI Engagement and Perceived Nutrition-Oriented Feeding Practices Among Urban Indonesian Mothers: Mixed Methods Study.
scored.why: This mixed methods study used partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine associations between generative artificial intelligence (AI) engagement and self-reported nutrition feeding practices among Indonesian mothers, mediated by cognitive empowerment and self-compassion. The study centers on attitudinal and psychological constructs rather than patient-clinician communication or clinical accuracy, making it largely off-topic for evaluating language models against clinicians.

scored.title: A Clinician-Centered Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models in Patient Education: Integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and Medical Condition Regard Scale.
scored.why: This viewpoint proposes a new clinician-centered evaluation framework, combining the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Medical Condition Regard Scale (MCRS), for assessing large language model (LLM)-generated patient education, but presents no empirical data or results. It is a proposed methodology rather than a finding, limiting its immediate relevance to the reader.

scored.title: From Hawai'i to the world: innovation, ultrasound, and leadership in perinatal medicine.
scored.why: This is a summit summary and editorial reflection on a perinatal medicine conference in Hawaii, discussing themes of ultrasound, artificial intelligence, and mentorship without presenting any original data or study. It contains no evaluable research finding and is not relevant to the reader's technical work.
